posts.title: Why everyone loves dividend?
posts.text: I’ve heard of ‘dividends’ long before I decided to learn about stock market, it seems like many people prefer ‘divdend-paying stock’. So it’s naturally to raise this question: what are dividends and why everyone loves them? DefinitionAccording to wiki, dividends are periodic payments made to shareholders from corporate profits. Reflected in the stock market, there are two kinds of distribution of dividends. Cash dividends. Pretty self-explanatory, we get cash. Stock dividends. Also self-explanatory, we get stocks.If that’s the only change, of course everyone loves them. However, when dividends happen, the stock price would fall proportionally. Take cash dividends as an example: suppose you have 10 shares at $10 each, and the genuine company decides to pay a dividend of $5 per share (seems too genuine), then you get $50 cash and 10 shares at $5 each. The asset value before and after cash dividends doesn’t change at all! For now, we leave this question for a while and we will come back to this topic in later chapters. ProcedureDuring a dividend payment procedure, there are 3 important dates. Record date. This is when the company records who can get the dividends. Every shareholder at this date can get dividends. Those who buy after this date can’t. Ex-Dividend date. This is when the stock price adjusts (minus dividend amount). Payment date. This is when people get paid in cash or in stocks.Apart from these dates, we also need to know about ‘Dividend Tax’, which charges from dividend amount. Usually, in order to encourage shareholders to invest for longer time, dividend tax get lower when people hold stocks for a longer period.
